headline: Shifts Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and associated infrastructure, preventing these costs from being passed on to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Dominion Energy, Governor Spanberger's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Pass Bills Shifting Data Center Energy Costs
news_summary: Virginia lawmakers passed legislation, including HB 1393, that shifts the cost of increased electric generating capacity and infrastructure to high-demand users like data centers, preventing these expenses from being passed to other customers. This move aims to address the significant energy consumption of data centers and its impact on the state's grid.

headline: Requires Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water utilities providing water to data centers report the total volume of water supplied, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board, enhancing transparency and aiding water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, water resource planners, local governments.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers
news_summary: Virginia's General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report the volume of water provided to data centers. This legislation, sponsored by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, aims to provide better data for policymakers and water resource planners to understand the industry's impact on the state's water resources.

headline: Establishes Data Center Siting and Noise Study Requirements
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate site assessments, including sound profiles, for new high-energy-use data centers (100 MW or more) near residential areas and schools, and allows for assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, environmental groups, local governments, community advocates.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce.
news_headline: Virginia Law Requires Data Center Noise and Siting Studies
news_summary: HB 153, now law, mandates that developers of large data centers conduct site assessments, including noise studies for nearby homes and schools, before local approval. While it requires studies, it does not set specific limits on noise or other impacts, leaving that to local discretion.
